Issued at 245 AM CDT Wed Sep 16 2026

TODAY AND TONIGHT...

High pressure was farther west than expected as of 07Z this 
morning, centered over southeast Manitoba. Winds remained light 
as opposed to being calm over much of the region, which was 
limiting our radiational cooling. Hibbing was at 38 degrees, 
International Falls was at 41, Cook was at 39, Bigfork was at 
40. Dewpoints were largely in the low 40s and upper 30s across 
the Northland. Will leave the Frost Advisory in place for this 
morning in Koochiching County though I suspect frost will be 
hard to come by.

Cloud cover over Wyoming, Colorado, Nebraska, and western South
Dakota associated with the next wave forecast to affect the 
Northland was evident on GOES-East Band 13 imagery early this 
morning. Isentropic ascent will spread into northern Minnesota 
and northwest Wisconsin through the day. Scattered showers will 
eventually develop. Rain chances begin late this afternoon and 
persist through tonight as the shortwave trough passes over the 
region aloft. Rainfall amounts will be relatively light, less 
than a tenth of an inch in general with a few spots along and 
south of WI-70 in Burnett, Washburn, Sawyer, and Price counties 
possibly picking up two tenths. Temperatures today will be 
warmest over central Minnesota east into northwest Wisconsin 
where cloud cover will arrive near/after peak heating. Highs 
will reach the low to middle 60s near the Canadian Border to the
low 70s in portions of northwest Wisconsin.

THURSDAY AND THURSDAY NIGHT...

Another area of surface high pressure will propagate from the 
northern Plains into the Canadian Prairies and northwest 
Ontario Thursday. Rain and cloud cover will depart to the east 
and south in the wake of today's shortwave trough. Highs 
Thursday will reach the middle 60s north to the middle 70s for 
portions of the St. Croix Valley in northwest Wisconsin.

FRIDAY AND SATURDAY...

A more substantive system will move from the central Plains 
into the Midwest Friday and Saturday. High pressure will retreat
eastward over Ontario into the Quebec. The waning influence of 
the departing high pressure will push dry air aloft southward 
over the Northland. Rain and perhaps a few thunderstorms will 
build northward into central Minnesota, the I-35 corridor, and 
northwest Wisconsin during the day in response to isentropic 
lift north of a surface warm front over southern Minnesota and 
southern Wisconsin. The dry air advecting from the north will 
undercut the showers and limit the northward extent of 
precipitation. It's likely we will see sharp gradient between 
light rain totals and accumulation of more than half an inch.

There remains a 30-80% chance of at least half an inch of rain 
generally south of a line from near Walker to Duluth and 
including all of northwest Wisconsin. Indicative of the tight 
gradient in QPF, the 30% or greater chances of an inch of rain 
are not much farther south than the half-inch values. Areas 
which have a 30% or greater chance of an inch of rain are south 
of a line from Pine River to Moose Lake to Mercer. Values 
greater than 80% are south of our area of responsibility. There 
is a small area of a 30-60% chance of 2 inches or more which is 
south of a line from Sandstone to near Hayward to Park Falls. 
The Weather Prediction Center included portions of Pine, 
Burnett, Washburn, Sawyer, and Price counties in a Slight Risk 
(Level 2 out of 4) of excessive rainfall. Area stream gauges 
revealed a small response from the rainfall on Monday. 
Therefore, if there are flash flooding concerns, they will 
likely be localized to areas where thunderstorms occur over low-
lying and poor drainage areas. Rain chances taper off from the 
pre-dawn hours of Saturday morning through Saturday afternoon 
from north to south.

Northeast winds over western Lake Superior will strengthen 
Friday, weaken slightly late Friday night and early Saturday 
morning, and strengthen again Saturday. The combination of wind 
and waves will increase the risk of rip currents at the beaches 
of the Twin Ports both days.

SUNDAY THROUGH NEXT WEDNESDAY...

Split flow aloft will propagate eastward over the northern 
Plains and Upper Midwest Sunday into Monday. Surface low 
pressure is forecast to develop and move through the Midwest 
which will bring at least modest rain chances to southern 
portions of the Northland. That low pressure will slowly move 
eastward and rain chances may persist into Tuesday.

A faster-moving trough is forecast to push into the northern 
Plains Tuesday afternoon and move across the Northland 
Wednesday. That wave will bring another chance of precipitation 
to the region.

Temperatures Sunday will start out a few degrees to the cool 
side of the normal range and gradually trend warmer by 
Wednesday. Look for highs in the middle to upper 60s Sunday and 
the upper 60s to low 70s by Wednesday.
